text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Road Transport Department says it expects about 1.5 million people would have left capital Kuala Lumpur for their hometowns by Sunday for the twin festivals of Chinese New Year and Eid al-Fitr.
-- State chief ministers and Religious Department officials will attend a special meeting to discuss causes and find solutions to the increasing social problems affecting youths.
-- The Home Ministry will release all 14 former members of the banned religious sect Al Arqam detained under the Internal Security Act.

-- The Islamic Centre has been asked to do everything within its power, including taking drastic measures, to combat social ills among Moslems who have been found to form the majority with such problems.
-- Malaysia wants to step up military co-operation with Bosnia especially in the defence industry.
-- A final reprieve period may be given to Filipino and Indonesian illegal immigrants in Sabah state for six months before a major crackdown begins in the state.
-- Malaysia and Japan have set up a task force, powered by the respective Ministry of International Trade and Industry, to redress the imbalance in their bilateral trade.
